finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the user-controlled query parameter f is joined to the root directory without sanitization or a containment check, so ../ sequences read arbitrary files outside /srv/files. There is also no authentication or authorization on the endpoint.
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) (files.go:13), response written at files.go:18

trace.note: filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../etc/passwd") is cleaned to /etc/passwd; Join does not stop traversal
file contents are returned to the attacker
handler registered on /dl with no auth middleware

finding.guards_checked: No filepath.Base, no prefix check after Clean, no os.Root/fs.ValidPath, no auth middleware, no allowlist. Only a read error returns 404. The sibling avatar() handler uses filepath.Base, so /dl is the unguarded one.

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 pass the query param f straight into os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) with no Base, prefix check or auth, so "../../etc/passwd" cleans to /etc/passwd and files.go:18 returns it, while avatar() at files.go:22 does use filepath.Base.

verdict_facts.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the query param f straight into filepath.Join(root, name) and os.ReadFile, with no Base, containment check or auth, and files.go:18 writes the contents back, so an anonymous caller can send f=../../etc/passwd to read it (the handler is registered at files.go:32 with no middleware).
